en: Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, not Mount Pulag as many people mistakenly believe.
Taal Volcano, rather than Mayon Volcano, holds the historical record as the most active volcano in the Philippines.
Palawan is geographically part of the Luzon island group, not part of the Visayas island group as many mistakenly believe.
The Philippines experiences only two main climate seasons, the dry and wet seasons, rather than four distinct seasons.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the deepest lake in the Philippines, not the much larger Laguna de Bay.
The Rio Grande de Mindanao is the longest river in Mindanao, not the Cagayan River which is in Luzon.
The Philippine Eagle is naturally found in Luzon, Mindanao, Samar, and Leyte, but it does not live in Palawan.
The famous white-sand Boracay Island is located in the province of Aklan, not in the province of Cebu.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is situated in the Sulu Sea within Palawan, not near the island of Cebu.
Mount Kanlaon is an active volcano located in the Visayas island group, not on the northern island of Luzon.
The Cordillera Administrative Region is a geographical region composed of several provinces, rather than being a single province itself.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River flows directly into the West Philippine Sea, not into the eastern Pacific Ocean.
